sanskrit: yātratā padasaṃghena smāryate yāgasādhanam / tāvadyajuśca vākyaṃ ca vaktavyatvānnirūpyate ekārthatvaṃ padasya myātmākāṅkṣāvayavaṃ na tat /
english: Now then, that which forms the meaning of the sentence in the Veda is the Bhavana, qualified by its accessories and differences in the Bhavana are always found to be cognised by such means as the presence of another word, and so forth vide next Pada. That is to say, in the case of a collection of words, where we do not find any other Bhāvanā expressed by such agencies as the presence of another word and so forth, we conclude that the sentence is one only and thus its multiplicity would always depend upon the denotation of other Bhāvanās. Consequently, inasmuch as both of thesesingleness and multiplicity are recognised by other means, the singleness of the sentence cannot be any reason for the singleness of the meaning.
